finding.title: V6 local-factor markout horizon is not bound to time-to-resolution
facts: Market metadata used by the local-factor model has no expiry/resolution field.
The intended hold is set from two residual half-lives, capped at 24, and converted to wall-clock time with a fixed 3600 seconds per bar.
The candidate expected residual change is one-step, while the intended hold can span many bars.
Therefore a local-factor bundle can schedule its modeled markout exit after the market has already resolved, where the assumed future bid/ask exit no longer exists.
The hold conversion is only dimensionally correct at the current 60-minute history fidelity.

deterministic_fixture.interpretation: This is a model-contract counterexample, not a live PnL estimate.

prerequisites: carry point-in-time expiry/resolution timestamp into V6 local-factor market metadata
use fidelity_minutes when converting AR half-life bars into wall-clock time
cap the markout hold at time-to-resolution minus a pre-resolution exit buffer
abstain when no valid pre-resolution markout window remains
use AR n-step expected residual change for the actual guarded hold horizon
keep terminal-probability modeling separate from markout relative value
combine with leave-one-out/cross-fitted factor estimation and dependence-aware unit-root inference before interpreting FDR
required_metrics: portfolio net PnL and drawdown at 1x/1.5x/2x executable costs

external_wiring_note: Do not duplicate the current V6 external startup fix: draft PR #272 already materializes the fail-closed approved q_external feed before starting the external engine. Current external evidence has zero passing direct terminal models, so the correct present feed remains abstention/header-only rather than fabricated probabilities.
